question: Which hardware or configuration upgrades does the measured load justify before the next stages on the new hosts?

measured_on.host: this-host-20260923 (adoption/hardware-profiles.json): Intel Core Ultra 9 275HX 24 threads, RTX 5090 Laptop GPU 24 GB, WSL2 with 48 GB configured (47 GB visible), 8 GB swap
measured_on.evidence_class: native_proven, point-in-time local measurement while five to eight agent sessions and a gap-resolution wave were running
measured_on.cpu: five 60-second samples of per-process utime+stime (2026-09-23 03:47-03:52 UTC): 1.1 to 9.9 of 24 cores busy per window; Gitleaks scans (no CPU cap) were 72% of all measured CPU (4.6, 8.4, 0.0, 1.9, 0.4 cores); all Claude sessions together about 0.5 cores; minute-bar collector about 0.2 cores
measured_on.gpu: 5.2 to 5.5 GiB of 23.9 GiB (24,463 MiB) in use; utilization median 6.5%, max 28% over 30 samples at 2 s (37% in one spot check); one resident model (Nemotron-3-Embed-1B at a 0.16 reservation); peak 20,217 MiB (19.7 GiB) when the qualified Qwen3-8B-AWQ worker ran beside it
measured_on.ram: 24 to 26 GiB available of 47 GiB visible; memory pressure (PSI some avg10) under 1; swap 0.9 of 8 GiB
measured_on.disk: 199 of 1081 GB used (df, decimal GB); growth is per-wave caches (about 44 GiB: 35 GiB and 8.6 GiB for the two current waves, du) and per-wave run state (about 21 GiB) with no retention rule
limits: One measurement window per quantity; short-lived jobs dominate single windows.
nvidia-smi cannot attribute VRAM per process under WSL; the embedder's share is its reservation.
The 128 GB workstation and the 48/64 GB macOS hosts are labelled projections until scripts/hardware_profile.py runs on each.
The raw CPU and GPU samples behind these figures are private to the measuring host's agent-lab records and are not retained in this repository.

items.change: Raise WSL memory from its default (half of physical RAM, 64 GB). The workstation runtime profile (docs/new-workstation-runtime-profile-20260922.md) proposes memory=96GB processors=60 swap=16GB.
items.evidence: adoption/hardware-profiles.json wsl-workstation-128gb-projected assumes wslconfig_memory_gb 100 and its 'headroom' semantic-RAG tier needs ram_gb >= 96; with the profiles' own arithmetic (about 1 GB of VM overhead) 96GB would show about 95 GB and miss that tier. The two records need reconciling by their owner; this manifest does not choose the value.

items.change: Give ecosystem-bounded-run a CPU property (CPUWeight or CPUQuota) so guarded scans cannot take many cores during interactive work.
items.owner: the lane that owns the ecosystem bin
items.evidence: Gitleaks was 72% of measured CPU, up to 8.4 cores in one window; the runner caps memory, swap, tasks and time but not CPU.

items.change: Archive per-wave run state and delete per-wave caches once the wave's record is closed.
items.evidence: about 65 GiB of per-wave caches and state (44 GiB caches, 21 GiB state) with no retention rule; 827 GB still free, so this is hygiene, not capacity.

items.change: A 48 GB or 96 GB workstation GPU, or a second GPU.
items.trigger: A selected local slot that does not fit 24 GB: a dense model above about 32B at 4 bits, or two 8B-class models resident with long contexts, or a measured throughput shortfall.
items.evidence: GPU utilization median 6.5%; the embedder plus the qualified 8B worker peaked at 20,217 MiB of 24,463 MiB; the generation tier for 24 GB is large-32b-q4.

items.trigger: Selecting a 150B-class mixture-of-experts model served partly from system RAM, after a measured throughput run shows it is usable. No such model is selected; runtime support for candidates such as MiMo-V2.6-Flash (159B) is unverified here.
items.evidence: RAM on the measured host has 24-26 GB free under full load; the workstation projection already reaches the 'headroom' tier at 100 GB.

items.change: More RAM for the 48 GB WSL laptop.
items.evidence: 24-26 GB available and memory pressure under 1 with five to eight sessions and a wave running.
827 GB free on the measured host; growth is addressed by the retention item.

items.change: No upgrade; use it as the portable host and for macOS acceptance.
items.evidence: Projected generation tier large-32b-q4 from about 38 GB of the 64 GB unified memory; no macOS workstation run exists yet, so acceptance, not hardware, is the open item.

items.change: Running trillion-parameter checkpoints locally (e.g. MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL, about 1.02T parameters, about 1 TB of weights).
items.evidence: Hugging Face API for XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL (queried 2026-09-23): safetensors total 1,024,216,603,392 parameters, mostly stored as U8 (about 1.0 TB); no listed host or upgrade reaches that memory. Such models are used through hosted APIs.

summary: Needed now: two software changes (bounded-run CPU limit, wave retention). Needed at setup: a larger WSL memory setting on the workstation (value to reconcile between the runtime profile and the hardware profiles). No hardware purchase is justified by the measured load; GPU memory is the upgrade to buy first if a selected local model outgrows 24 GB.
